title: Fisher, Brunus and other uptown players; the Lane neighbor
summary: He doesn't know Fisher, Schilling or Tom Brown; he mentions a neighbor Lane and a deceased brother who played trombone.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Do you remember uh Fisher's band? It was a band run by I think it was Johnny Fisher. Do you remember, I think that was uptown, that might have been in the Irish channel up that way. Maybe so. Fisher, do you remember hearing him? No. Did you ever know any of the Brunus family? Brunus.
Brunus. Up there in the Irish channel? Yeah. Well they, they had a band I believe of Brunus.

Did you ever play with any of those fellas? Richard Brunus, Henry Brunus? No, never did. I wondered uh Happy Schilling, do you remember Happy Schilling, a trombone player? No, I don't remember him either. He was uptown too. And uh Tom Brown, do you remember Tom Brown?

No, I don't know nothing of him either. You don't remember? No, this man lives next door here, Mr. Lane, he had a brother they buried him a few years ago. He used to be a good trombone player too. Oh yeah, which uh Julian Lane?

Julian Lane. Julian Lane. Julian, yeah. Julian, yeah. Yeah, he's about two years now, I think he's dead. No, he's brother. Oh, I mean in the other house? In the half house, yeah. Does his brother play any instruments?
No. He doesn't play any instruments?

He's working out there on Tulane Avenue in that big uh uh uh St. Clair and there's three of them mixed up in that big factory they think. They fixed up machinery and patron makers I think and so on. Yeah, the patron makers. Well that's where he was and that's that's his son I'll tell you about.
